transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I suppose what brings me in is that I’ve been hearing things, voices really. Clear voices in my apartment, and sometimes in empty rooms at the museum. It sounds like women whispering from behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive. I know that probably sounds odd, but… that’s been happening, and I thought I should mention it.
Do you believe someone or something is deliberately causing these voices?

I mean… I don’t want to sound paranoid or difficult. But yes, I do think there’s something deliberate going on. I’ve felt pretty sure the museum board and some of the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. They know my Caribbean archive could change the way the galleries tell the truth, and… no one has really shown me anything that proves they aren’t involved. Does that make sense to say?
Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high or energized for days at a time?

Yes… I suppose there have been times like that. I try not to make too much of it, because sometimes it feels like a good thing, like I’m radiant, or chosen for something important. But if someone questions what I’m doing, or tells me I need to slow down, I can get… very angry. Furious, really. It feels like they’re trying to erase me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have the voices ever happened during a time when your mood felt completely normal?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I wasn’t especially energized or feeling grand at that point—not like those other times. For a few weeks I felt more or less normal, or as normal as I get, I suppose. But I was still hearing the whispering in my apartment, and I still felt pretty sure the arts people were monitoring my phone. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Have you used any drugs or substances around the times when the voices started?
No… not that I can think of. I mean, I don’t use drugs, and I wasn’t taking anything like that when the voices started. I hope that’s the sort of thing you mean.
Have you found yourself becoming much less interested in seeing people or doing things you used to care about?

Yes… though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. There are stretches where I just sort of sit at my kitchen table, and the little herb pots will be drying out, and I still don’t quite get up to deal with them.

And I don’t always call friends back. Even if someone invites me to a concert or a gallery opening—things I used to care about—I’ll think, “That sounds nice,” but I don’t really feel pulled toward it. I suppose that counts, doesn’t it?
Did the voices and the feeling that people were monitoring you begin very suddenly, over a day or two?

No… I don’t think it was quite that sudden. It’s hard to pin down exactly, but the voices and that feeling that people are watching my archive have been going on for… about eight months now. It sort of built into something I was sure about, if that makes sense.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d call it that, exactly. I do have low spells, but whether it’s most of the day nearly every day for two full weeks… I’d have to think. I don’t want to overstate it. I suppose I’ve felt down at times, but I’m not sure it fits the way you’re asking.
During those times when you felt radiant or chosen, did you need much less sleep than usual?

Yes… I suppose I did. Not in a bad way, at least it didn’t feel bad at the time. I could sleep maybe two or three hours and then wake up before dawn feeling completely ready, almost pleased with myself.

I’d tell myself, well, sleep is for people who don’t have an archive to rescue. That sounds a bit much when I say it out loud, doesn’t it? But at the time it felt very clear.
Have you ever had a period when that unusually high or energized mood lasted at least a week?

Yes… I think so. More than a week, really. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but those stretches where I had all that energy and all the plans going at once… they weren’t just a day or two.

If I’m being honest, off and on, that kind of state has taken up maybe six months of this whole period. The little sleep, feeling driven, spending more than I should… it felt productive at the time, not like an “episode,” if that makes sense. But yes, it lasted well over a week.
Have you ever heard the voices during a time when you were feeling depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I… I’m not sure it lines up only with being depressed, if that’s okay to say. The voices are more what brought me in, really. I hear them pretty clearly in my apartment, and sometimes in empty museum rooms… like women whispering from behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive.

I know that sounds strange. I don’t mean that I’m trying to make it into something bigger than it is, but yes, I do hear them.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voices or felt monitored while your mood was completely normal—not high, energized, or depressed?

Yes… I think there was. I almost don’t want to say “completely normal,” because I’m not always the best judge of that, but there were several weeks where I wasn’t especially up or grand, and I wasn’t terribly low either.

I was just… ordinary, more or less. But I still heard the whispering in the apartment. And I still felt quite sure the arts people were keeping an eye on my phone. I know that may sound excessive, but it didn’t feel connected to my mood then. It was just there.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I don’t know that I could honestly say that, no. I’ve had sad days, of course, and times I felt discouraged, but “most of the day, nearly every day” for two weeks… I’m not sure I’ve noticed it that way.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer just to be helpful. It doesn’t stand out to me as a clear period like that.
During the past eight months, have the voices and the feeling of being monitored been present for most of that time, even when your mood was not unusually high or depressed?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to overstate it, but the voices, and that certainty that people are watching my archive, have been there for about eight months now.

Even when my mood wasn’t especially high or low, it was still… present. Most of the time, I’d say. Does that answer it the right way?
